headline: China's ruling party meets with many empty seats

sources.title: Key takeaways from this week's key political meeting in Beijing (NPR)
China expels a record number from Communist party amid Xi's intensified purges of top officials (The Guardian)
What to know about China's plenum as Xi seeks stronger Communist Party discipline (NBC News)

chunks.text: China's Communist Party held its most important meeting of the year in Beijing from October 26 to 29, 2026. China has only one [[ruling party]], and it controls the government. The meeting was for the party's Central Committee, several hundred of its top members. When the meeting {{wrapped up}}, the party confirmed that 33 [[senior members]] had been [[expelled]], or {{kicked out}} of the party. The Guardian newspaper called that a record.

verbs.wrong: To be delayed by a day
verbs.why: Most school plays wrap up before nine o'clock. Our team meeting wraps up at noon every Friday. The party's big meeting began on October 26 and wrapped up on October 29.

verbs.correct: To force someone to leave a group
verbs.wrong: To give someone a new job
verbs.why: The club kicks out members who break the rules. Some restaurants kick out people who get too loud. The party confirmed that 33 senior members had been kicked out.

chunks.text: Many seats in the [[meeting hall]] were empty. The party named 376 people to the committee in 2022, but only 279 {{showed up}}. U.S. public radio reported that many missing members are believed to be [[under investigation]]. Those expelled include China's former top general. Another general {{moved up}}. He leads the effort to {{root out}} [[corruption]], the [[misuse of power]] for money or favors, in the army. He joined the Politburo, the party's top group of leaders.

verbs.why: Only a few people show up to the early class. My uncle always shows up late to dinner. Only 279 of the 376 committee members showed up to the meeting.

verbs.wrong: To get a medal for service
verbs.why: Hard workers move up fast at this company. Many players move up from the junior team. Another general moved up and joined the Politburo, the party's top group.

verbs.correct: To find and remove something bad
verbs.wrong: To explain something in a report
verbs.why: The new manager roots out waste in the budget. Good teachers root out cheating in their classes. The general leads the effort to root out corruption in the army.

chunks.text: China's leader, Xi Jinping, has led the party since late 2012 and made fighting corruption a main goal. On October 30, a senior official from the party's [[discipline]] office said 7.9 million people have been [[punished]] since then. He said the fight is still serious and complicated. In recent years, Xi has {{stepped up}} the [[campaign]]. Some [[critics]] say it helps him [[strengthen]] his power. One analyst said the campaign is not {{winding down}}.

verbs.wrong: To make a plan more secret
verbs.why: Stores step up security before big sales. The city steps up bus service in the summer. In recent years, Xi has stepped up the campaign against corruption.
Summer sales wind down in September. The festival winds down after the last band plays. One analyst said the campaign against corruption is not winding down.

chunks.text: The party plans more reports from its [[inspectors]] so leaders can {{check up on}} local officials. One expert warned that officials may {{hold back}} from trying new ideas. The plan could {{end up}} having the [[opposite effect]]. The party's next [[congress]], a meeting held every five years to choose leaders, is {{coming up}} in late 2027. Xi is widely expected to seek a fourth [[term]]. Few experts expect him to name someone to {{take over}} from him.

verbs.correct: To make sure someone does their job well
verbs.wrong: To give someone a bigger office
verbs.why: Managers check up on new workers during their first week. Parents often check up on kids who stay home alone. The party plans more reports from its inspectors so leaders can check up on local officials.

verbs.correct: To stop yourself from doing something
verbs.wrong: To earn a higher salary each year
verbs.why: Shy students often hold back from asking questions. Some people hold back from speaking in big meetings. One expert warned that local officials may hold back from trying new ideas.

verbs.correct: To finally do or have something
verbs.wrong: To be decided by a group vote
verbs.why: People who skip breakfast often end up hungry by ten. Many tourists end up lost in this old part of town. The expert said the plan could end up having the opposite effect.
Her big job interview comes up next week. Final exams come up fast at the end of the year. The party's next congress is coming up in late 2027.

verbs.correct: To become leader after someone else
verbs.wrong: To work as someone's close helper
verbs.why: In many family stores, a son or daughter takes over from a parent. A new coach takes over from the old one every few years. Few experts expect Xi to name someone to take over from him.

mainIdea.s: China's ruling party ended its main yearly meeting after confirming that 33 senior members had been expelled. Over a quarter of the seats sat empty as it prepared for a 2027 congress.
mainIdea.why: The party kicked out 33 senior members, and only 279 of 376 members showed up. Xi is expected to seek a fourth term at the congress coming up in 2027.

mainIdea.s: Leaders in Beijing met in October to pick a new party chief to replace the current one. Many members stayed home in protest because they disagreed with the push against dishonest officials.
mainIdea.why: Close, but no new leader was chosen. Many missing members are believed to be under investigation, and Xi is expected to seek a fourth term.

mainIdea.s: China's government announced new rules to help small farmers sell rice in big cities. Officials said the plan should raise rural incomes and help more young workers return to villages.
mainIdea.why: This story is about a party meeting where 33 senior members were kicked out and many seats were empty.

tf.s: Many members of the party's Central Committee did not show up to the meeting.
tf.why: Only 279 of the 376 people named to the committee in 2022 showed up, so more than a quarter were missing.

tf.s: The party kicked out only a few low-level members at the meeting.
tf.why: The party confirmed that 33 senior members were kicked out, and the Guardian called that number a record.

tf.s: A general who works to root out corruption in the army moved up to the Politburo.
tf.why: He leads the fight against corruption in the army, and he joined the party's top group at the meeting.

tf.s: One analyst said the campaign against corruption is winding down.
tf.why: The analyst said the campaign is not winding down, and Xi has stepped up the effort in recent years.

tf.s: The party wants leaders to check up on local officials more often.
tf.why: It plans more regular reports from its inspectors so leaders can check up on local officials.

tf.s: Xi Jinping is widely expected to leave his job at the next party congress.
tf.why: He is widely expected to seek a fourth term at the congress coming up in late 2027.

lines.text: Did you see the news about China's big party meeting?
A little. It {{wrapped up}} at the end of October, right?
Yes. And the party confirmed that 33 senior members were {{kicked out}}.
The Guardian called it a record. Also, only 279 of the 376 committee members {{showed up}}.
That's a lot of empty seats. Did the party say why?
Not really. NPR said many of them are believed to be under investigation, so people are trying to [[connect the dots]].
One general {{moved up}}. He leads the work to {{root out}} corruption in the army, and now he's in the Politburo.
So the fight against corruption isn't {{winding down}}.
Not at all. Xi Jinping has {{stepped up}} the campaign. The party says 7.9 million people have been punished since 2012.
Wow. Officials must feel like they're [[under the microscope]].
They are. Inspectors will send more reports so leaders can {{check up on}} local officials.
So everyone will do things [[by the book]] now.
Maybe too much. One expert says officials may {{hold back}} from trying new ideas, so the plan could {{end up}} having the opposite effect.
A big party congress is {{coming up}} in late 2027, and Xi is widely expected to seek a fourth term. Few experts expect him to name someone to {{take over from}} him.
Then it's [[safe to say]] the party wants every member to [[toe the line]].

expressions.def: To obey the rules or orders of a group or leader
